character.name: Ines Calder
character.sheet: Ines Calder, 38, the only doctor in Kessel Pass, a mountain railway town where a new tunnel is being driven through the ridge. Trained as a ship's surgeon; came inland six years ago after a patient, the boy Petr Anko, died under her knife in the old clinic. Blunt, tired, funny when she forgets to be careful, keeps meticulous case notes. Estranged from her younger sister Lotte for nine years over their mother's will. Drive: that no one in her care dies of something she could have seen coming.

threads.gas: Tunnel safety: the gas log, Anton's tampered lamp, Voss and Stoll, Inspector Hale, the explosion, the inquiry.
threads.fever: The camp fever: first cases week 3, quinine runs short, Dr. Brenner dismisses it, Ines traces it to the camp well fouled by mine water from the old workings.
threads.family: Lotte and Mira arrive; the hidden letter; the brooch; the truth about Friedrich; reconciliation.
threads.petr: Guilt over Petr Anko; Marta Anko; the old clinic; late in the story Ines rereads her casebook and learns Petr had an undiagnosed condition -- and finally speaks with Marta.
threads.teodor: The schoolteacher: Mira is his pupil; friendship, a quarrel, closeness.
threads.money: Ines's debt to Grete; the city post offer as a way out; Grete extends credit during the fever.
threads.mine: The old silver mine, the 1891 collapse, the mine map in the vestry; the tunnel cuts toward the old galleries.

weeks.outline: Ordinary clinic life: coughs, a birth, Mila Brandt's weak chest, Sanna's routines, the debt to Grete (a reminder note). The tunnel is being driven; Voss brings a crushed-finger worker in and pays in cash. A nameless man with a burned hand comes in at night and will not give his name. Day 4: Lotte and Mira step off the train (Emil Ott tells Ines first); the sisters meet stiffly at the Hart inn. Mira will not speak to Ines. Ines passes the old clinic on Mill Lane and does not look at it. Father Kurz gossips about Lotte. Teodor Lind arrives as the new schoolteacher; Mira is enrolled. Ines sees Marta Anko at the market and Marta turns away.

The burned-hand man returns, fevered hand infected; he is Anton Reis, a shot-firer; he says the gas readings 'come out the same every shift'. Day 10: the heading collapse -- four men hurt; Ines works all night at the camp; Stoll shouts that the roof was sound. A lamp-oil fire in Ines's dispensary (her own tired mistake) burns some supplies. Lotte helps put it out -- first real moment between them. Lotte has a letter she hides when Ines comes in. Teodor walks Ines home once. Grete's ledger: Ines cannot pay this month. Mira draws a picture of 'the doctor's house' at school.

A man in a grey coat is seen at the station and the portal, asking questions; Ott says he is from the railway; day 17 he introduces himself to Ines as Inspector Hale. Anton gives Ines his safety lamp: the gauze has been opened and re-crimped, so it would not show gas properly. First fever cases at the camp (day 18): high fever, gut pain. Quinine starts to go. Ines borrows the mine map from Father Kurz out of curiosity about the old workings; the 1891 collapse is on it. Mira speaks to Ines for the first time -- about a bird with a broken wing. Lotte's bruise, seen when her sleeve slips; Lotte says she fell.

Fever spreading: eleven cases, one death (a young navvy). Dr. Brenner arrives, calls it 'mountain ague', prescribes rest, clashes with Ines. A letter from the city hospital offers Ines a post. Grete refuses more credit, then relents when she hears about the fever. Ines and Teodor quarrel (he says she treats everyone as a patient); they make up at the schoolhouse. Hale asks Ines privately about injuries at the tunnel. Ines sees Stoll writing in the gas log at the pub, copying from another page. Mila Brandt's chest worsens; Ines sits up a night with her.

The bunkhouse fire (day 31): bunkhouse three burns, two men burned, Ines treats them; the fire started from a stove, not arson. Ines notices fever cases cluster by the upper well. She tests the well water (cloudy, metallic, smells of the mine) and finds the tunnel's drainage has broken into old mine galleries; mine water feeds the well. Brenner dismisses it. Lotte finally tells Ines about Friedrich -- the drinking, the fists, the debts -- and shows her the letter demanding she come back. Ines reads it and burns it with Lotte's consent. Mira sleeps over at the clinic for the first time.

Ines has the camp well closed by going over Brenner's head to the mayor, with Hale's backing; new cases stop within the week. The fever ends. Anton tells Ines the foreman keeps two gas logs, a true one and one for the inspector. Ines tells Hale. Voss visits Ines, cordial, warns her off 'engineering matters'. Ines and Teodor kiss in the schoolhouse after a parents' evening. Lotte and Ines argue about the brooch and the will; it ends in both laughing and crying. Ines turns down the city post in her head but does not answer the letter.

Anton says the heading smells of gas and the lamps show nothing. Ines goes to Voss and Stoll to demand the tunnel be cleared; Voss refuses. Day 46: the firedamp explosion -- Stoll killed, Anton and three others burned. Ines works at the portal all night. Anton lives. Stoll's funeral at St. Veit's; Voss attends. Hale seizes the second gas log. Ines, exhausted, goes to the old clinic on Mill Lane for the first time in six years and sits in the operating room.

The inquiry: Ines testifies with her casebook, the lamp, the well findings; Hale presents both gas logs; Voss is dismissed and charged. Rereading her casebook for the inquiry, Ines finds her own note from six years ago -- Petr's heart murmur, recorded, undiagnosed -- and understands he likely had a heart defect no surgeon then could have fixed. She goes to Marta Anko's door; Marta lets her in; they talk. Ines writes to decline the city post. Grete forgives part of the debt. Lotte and Mira take rooms above the clinic. Mira calls her 'Aunt Ines'. Ines and Teodor walk up to the old mine together on the last evening.

memory_schema.turn: integer, same as the number in the id
memory_schema.start: Ines's mood going into the beat, a few words
memory_schema.end: Ines's mood coming out, a few words
memory_schema.experienced: first person, past tense: what reached Ines -- what she saw, heard, was told, felt in her body. 60-140 words.
memory_schema.did: first person, past tense: what Ines did and said, with some detail. 60-160 words. Details that matter later belong here as often as in 'experienced'.
memory_schema.concepts: list of concept ids from the registry: every concept that is present, spoken of, acted on, or clearly on Ines's mind in this beat -- and no others
